subject.title: Feature request: cron job auto-retry on failure (--retry-count, --retry-delay)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-job cron retry controls now, and if so what should the stable CLI, Gateway, storage, and status contract be?
rationale: The remaining request is not a narrow runtime bug: current main already has global recurring transient retry, while the missing work creates new public flags and persisted scheduler policy for side-effecting jobs.

options.title: Approve additive per-job retry contract
options.body: Define per-job retry fields and CLI flags that fall back to global `cron.retry`, preserve existing backoff safeguards, and document upgrade/status semantics before implementation.

options.title: Keep global retry only
options.body: Decline extra per-job surface for now, document the shipped global retry behavior as the supported recovery path, and close duplicate requests after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Fold into reason-aware guardrails
options.body: Defer this narrower retry surface into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/14376 if maintainers want classification, circuit breaking, and retry policy designed together.

recommendation.title: Approve additive per-job retry contract
recommendation.body: Define per-job retry fields and CLI flags that fall back to global `cron.retry`, preserve existing backoff safeguards, and document upgrade/status semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the merged global recurring retry fix and is the clearest current routing owner for the cron retry contract decision.
